nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be pairwise distinct positive real numbers. Then at most one of the equations $a^2 = bc$, $b^2 = ac$ and $c^2 = ab$ holds; that is, no two of them hold simultaneously.
nodes.title: At most one square is the product of the other two

nodes.summary: Every MPTQ set whose elements are all positive real numbers has at least $8$ elements.
nodes.title: Chu's bound for MPTQ sets of positive reals

nodes.summary: Every MPTQ set of real numbers that contains a negative number has at least $5$ elements.
nodes.title: Chu's bound for MPTQ sets with a negative element

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of positive real numbers and $-A = \{-a : a \in A\}$. Then $A \cup (-A)$ is an MPTQ set if and only if $A$ is an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: Adjoining negatives preserves the MPTQ property

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of integers and $p$ a prime number such that every element of $A$ is coprime to $p$, and let $pA = \{pa : a \in A\}$. Regarding sets of integers as sets of real numbers, $A \cup pA$ is an MPTQ set if and only if $A$ is an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: Adjoining multiples by a coprime prime preserves the MPTQ property

nodes.summary: A finite set $A$ of real numbers is an MPTQ (more products than quotients) set when $0 \notin A$ and $|A/A| < |A \cdot A|$, where $A \cdot A = \{ab : a, b \in A\}$ is the product set, $A/A = \{a/b : a, b \in A\}$ is the quotient set, and $|X|$ is the number of elements of $X$.
nodes.title: MPTQ set

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a set of eight integers, regarded as a set of real numbers, and let $S = \{0, 2, 3, 4, 7, 11, 12, 14\}$. Then $A$ is an MSTD set if and only if $A = \{as + b : s \in S\}$ for some integers $a \neq 0$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Hegarty's classification of MSTD sets of size eight

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be pairwise distinct positive real numbers with $ab = cd$. Then $ad \neq bc$ and $ac \neq bd$.
nodes.title: One equal pairing of products excludes the other two

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of real numbers that is not an MPTQ set, let $x$ be a real number, let $n \le m$ be natural numbers, and write $A' = A \cup \{x\}$. If $|A' \cdot A'| \le |A \cdot A| + n$ and $|A/A| + m \le |A'/A'|$, where $X \cdot X$ and $X/X$ denote the product set and quotient set of $X$, then $A'$ is not an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: Adjoining an element that adds no more products than quotients

nodes.summary: No set of five real numbers is an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: No MPTQ set has five elements

nodes.summary: If $A$ is a set of five real numbers exactly one of which is negative, then $A$ is not an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: Five-element sets with one negative element are not MPTQ sets

nodes.summary: If $A$ is a set of five real numbers exactly two of which are negative, then $A$ is not an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: Five-element sets with two negative elements are not MPTQ sets

nodes.summary: If $A$ is a finite set of real numbers with $0 \in A$, then $A$ is not an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: Sets containing zero are not MPTQ sets

nodes.summary: For every real number $a$, the one-element set $\{a\}$ is not an MPTQ set.
nodes.title: A singleton is not an MPTQ set

nodes.summary: No set of seven integers, viewed as a set of real numbers, is an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Hegarty: no seven-element MSTD set of integers
